newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B index ends slightly up in wary mood.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B index ends slightly up in wary mood.

text.p: The Shanghai B share index ended slightly up on Wednesday on selective speculative buying spurred by sharp rises on the A share market, brokers said.
But a cautious mood still dominated the market on concerns about a possible new official crackdown on market volatility, they said.
The B index edged up 0.007 points or 0.01 percent to 73.327 on volume of 18.59 million shares worth $9.1 million.
The A index put on 42.496 points or 3.25 percent to 1,349.527 on turnover of 11.9 billion yuan.
Brokers said that bargain-hunting emerging late in the session reversed early losses, but overseas investors still remained on the sidelines with the 1996 results of most firms still to be released.
Only seven of 43 B share listed firms have so far issued their results with the April 30 deadline of April 30 approaching.
Of 43 B shares, 42 traded, with 15 up, 10 flat and 17 down.
Shanghai Lianhua Fibre was the star on speculative buying, jumping $0.012 or 6.06 percent to $0.210 on volume of 1,000 shares.
Huangshan Tourism was the second biggest gainer on expectations of good earnings, up $0.032 or 5.17 percent to $0.650 on volume of 1.4 million shares.
China First Pencil traded the most on institutional selling, down $0.002 or 0.42 percent to $0.464 on volume of 2.5 million shares.
The Shanghai A share index surged despite Beijing's recent warnings to the market over investment risks. A speculative mood prevailed with hot money continuing to flow into the market, brokers said.
The SSE30 index rose 88.118 points or 2.54 percent to 3,560.416 points.
Changan Information was the star on speculative buying, surging 0.95 yuan or 10.05 percent to 10.40 yuan on volume of 4.2 million shares.
